headline: Town engineer recommended two turfgrass fields for the Hamden Middle School field replacement, estimated at $9.5 million for full build-out.
summary: The meeting covered a Middle School field replacement plan, with a full build-out of about $9.5 million and a partial scope of $4,624,179. The town engineer recommends two turfgrass fields. Updates were also given on HHS tennis court repairs and other old business, with no final decisions recorded on those items.
decisions: Town engineer recommended two turfgrass fields in the Middle School field plan, which has a full build-out of about $9.5 million.
Approved unanimously a motion to reject the September 9th, 2026 minutes in order to amend them.

TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Parks & Recreation Commission 
Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
7:00 PM, October 13, 2026 
 
 
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
 
• Chairman Francese called the meeting to order at 7:06 PM; Commissioner Arny 
seconded the motion. 
 
2. ATTENDANCE 
  
 
• In attendance: Dominic Francese, Chair, Commissioners, Ryan Ott, Arny Mann, 
Richard Leonardo, Katyayani Mishra, Youth Commissioner, Karen Bivens, Director, 
Cultural Affairs & Human Services Parks & Recs Director, and Steven White, the 
Town Engineer. 
 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 
• Chairman Francese motioned to reject the minutes from September 9th, 2026, in 
order to amend them. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Leandro and 
approved unanimously.  
 
4. PUBLIC COMMENT 
  
 
• None 
 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
There will be a brief summary of the correspondence submitted between the last 
correspondence update and this one. This includes but is not limited to any 
correspondence with council members that members wish to submit for the record. It can 
also include written communication to the council from the administration, community 
members, etc.
None 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 
• Not needed. 
 
7. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  1. Hamden Middle School field replacement plan (Hamden Town Engineer Stephen 
White scheduled to attend and present). 
   
  
• The proposed plan for a full build-out is about $9.5 million, including installing 
two new turfgrass fields, and repairing middle school tennis courts. The cost 
for a partial scope comes up to $4,624,179. Both options will keep the field 
inaccessible for a long period of time, but the town engineer recommends two 
turfgrass fields. 
 
  2. Update on HHS tennis court repair/replacement.  
  
• The deadline for a final proposal package with USTA requirements is expected 
around May 2027. Courts will be of asphalt using $150K from Quinnipiac, and 
$250K from USTA, as well as $500K from local capital. 
 
8. REPORTS 
  
 
• An assessment of the middle school fields shows that heavy use by recreation 
leagues has contributed to the field's deterioration. While the irrigation system is 
installed, it is not functional. 
• Potential solutions include reconditioning all grass fields, redoing drainage and 
irrigation systems as necessary, as well as regrading the fields while at the same 
time repaving the exterior walking paths. 
• The proposed plan for a full build-out is about $9.5 million, including installing two 
new turfgrass fields, and repairing middle school tennis courts. The cost for a partial 
scope comes up to $4,624,179. Both options will keep the field inaccessible for a 
long period of time, but the town engineer recommends two turfgrass fields. 
• Environmental concerns exist for turfgrass fields, but they can be mitigated by 
material selection. 
• The tennis courts will be of asphalt using $150K from Quinnipiac, and $250K from 
USTA, as well as a local $500K capital fund. The deadline for the final proposal 
package with USTA requirements is expected around May 2027.
1.  
Director of Cultural Affairs and Human Services, Karen Bivens to briefly report 
on activities of the Parks and Recreation department.  
  
•  
 
  
9. OLD BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  1. BOE Facility use fees for town-sponsored programs (status of negotiations between 
Mayor and BOE).   
  
 
  2. Rochford Field contract (status of discussions between Mayor and Albertus). 
   
  
• Public works and the engineer are currently assessing the overall use of 
Rochefort and whether it could be isolated for Albertus. 
• There is a drainage issue that often requires the parks crew to have to drain 
the field for it to be playable.  
• A request to obtain a full schedule was made in order to better coordinate 
lighting on the field.  
 
  3. League stipends (status of requests).   
  
• Stipends have been distributed for baseball. Still awaiting the requests from 
football, Heroness’s and lacrosse. 
 
  4. Ice rink Committee (update by Dominic and Arnie from the first two meetings).   
  
• The Rink Committee was joined by Joe Colello for an assessment of how it is 
run and its long-term needs in terms of capital improvements. 
• The finance department will provide models and recommendations in early 
January. 
• Commissioner Ryan Ott suggested exploring an open bid competition in the 
planned RFP to ensure that the town and its citizens are well served. 
• On October 22nd, the BOE and Hamden Athletics will be visiting the rink, 
followed by Parks & Recs in November.
• Recommendation to vote on a new schedule for next year's commission 
meetings, and perhaps, considering moving the meetings to 5:30 PM. The 
new voted schedule would be submitted to the Clerk’s office.  
10. ADJOURNMENT 
  
 
• The motion to adjourn was introduced at 8:58 PM, seconded by Commissioner Arny, 
and was approved unanimously.
